blocks.text: **The problem.** Given `n`, return how many **structurally different** binary search trees hold exactly the values 1 to n.

blocks.alt: The five BSTs on the values 1, 2 and 3. With root 1 the other two values form a 2-node right subtree, which has 2 shapes. With root 2, 1 goes left and 3 goes right: 1 shape. With root 3, 2 shapes on the left. Total 2 + 1 + 2 = 5.

elements.text: n = 3: pick the root, then count the shapes on each side
elements.originalText: n = 3: pick the root, then count the shapes on each side

blocks.text: Choose the root value r. Then 1..r−1 must form the left subtree and r+1..n the right one, and any left shape combines with any right shape. The number of shapes depends only on **how many** values a side has, not which ones. So with G(k) = the number of BSTs on k values:

blocks.code:
G(0) = 1                      (the empty tree is one shape)
G(n) = sum over r = 1..n of  G(r - 1) * G(n - r)

blocks.text: **Time O(3ⁿ)** — the same G(k) is recomputed over and over — **space O(n).**

blocks.caption: G[k] is filled from smaller sizes: every root splits k values into a left and a right part.

blocks.code:
def num_trees(n):
    G = [0] * (n + 1)
    G[0] = 1
    G[1] = 1
    for k in range(2, n + 1):             # k values
        for r in range(1, k + 1):
            G[k] += G[r - 1] * G[k - r]
    return G[n]

blocks.text: G(n) = C(2n, n) / (n + 1), and successive Catalan numbers satisfy G(i+1) = G(i) · 2(2i + 1) / (i + 2). Multiply before dividing — the division is always exact.
**Time O(n), space O(1).** Use 64-bit numbers: the product before dividing outgrows 32 bits long before the answer does.

rows.timeWhy: The same **G(k)** is recomputed over and over by different branches.
Each of the **n** entries sums over up to **n** root choices.
